_readme: Custom template patterns for /template-maps (L-018/P-7): a template authored as a small TILE of cell roles ('' void, '1' floor, '1s' floor slot, '2' platform, '2s' podium slot, '3s' high podium slot, '4' wall), applied to painted zones by repeat / halfdrop / stamp. Author new ones in /template-pattern-editor. Seeded 2026-07-15.

uffizi-spine-enfilade.label: Uffizi U-Spine Enfilade
uffizi-spine-enfilade.walk_rule: Enter at the head of the east spine and walk the 3-wide corridor pulled forward by the hero visible on-axis 27 cells ahead, dipping optionally through door gaps into three side rooms whose aligned doors form a second parallel vista, then turn west along the south corridor past the hero and exit on the enfilade axis.
uffizi-spine-enfilade.pacing_rule: Paired podium statues line the spine's inner wall in bays broken by door gaps (Vasari's three-bays-plus-narrow-bay rhythm), and every pause option sits off the clear lane so lingering never dams the flow; the one mandated stop is the raised dais step before the end-stopped hero.

guggenheim-serpentine.label: Guggenheim Switchback — spiral as serpentine descent
guggenheim-serpentine.museum: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York
guggenheim-serpentine.walk_rule: Enter at the top (the elevator drop-off) and walk one un-branching serpentine: each 3-wide lane runs the full width, turns through a 3-cell gap at the alternating end of each partition, and empties onto the rotunda floor at the bottom where the hero stands on the atrium axis.
guggenheim-serpentine.pacing_rule: Movement never pauses the route — art bays are recessed into the solid partition stretches as stop pockets beside the flow, while the aligned see-through void windows (c6-c8) form the atrium axis that promises the hero podium from up to 27 cells away and re-shows passed works across lanes.

neue-nationalgalerie-free-plan.label: Mies Free-Plan Hall
neue-nationalgalerie-free-plan.walk_rule: Enter anywhere on the open top edge and drift freely through a column-free field; freestanding picture-walls and podia are obstacles to orbit, not corridors to follow, and the only fixed event is the on-axis hero at the hall's centre.
neue-nationalgalerie-free-plan.pacing_rule: Pacing comes from paired off-axis freestanding walls at each third of the walk that slow the drift into eddies, while the untouched central axis keeps a 13-cell promise to the hero so the visitor always chooses between lingering and advancing.

soane-cabinet-vista.label: Soane Cabinet — dense pockets on an end-stopped axis
soane-cabinet-vista.museum: Sir John Soane's Museum, 13 Lincoln's Inn Fields, London
soane-cabinet-vista.walk_rule: A 3-wide spine runs the full axis while staggered door gaps pull the body sideways into small 3x4 cabinet pockets; the eye keeps the long axial vista to the hero as the feet loop room by room.
soane-cabinet-vista.pacing_rule: Every five rows a cross-wall with corridor-facing niche slots compresses the walk back onto the spine, alternating pocket-dwell and corridor-glide, until the terminal dome room releases the width and the hero end-stops the 16-cell sightline just before a blind wall.

castelvecchio-endstopped-enfilade.label: Castelvecchio End-Stopped Enfilade
castelvecchio-endstopped-enfilade.walk_rule: Enter on the central axis and cross four rooms through aligned 3-wide door gaps; in each room the works sit off-axis so you drift sideways to a stop pocket and return to the line, until the axis delivers you into the hero bay where you circle the raised podium and exit through the off-axis side door behind it.
castelvecchio-endstopped-enfilade.pacing_rule: The hero is visible from the entrance through every aligned gap (a 24-cell promise), but four cross walls each impose a pause-and-drift beat before the axis is allowed to resolve, and the end-stop wall plus sideways exit ensure the vista terminates on the hero instead of continuing past it.

grande-galerie-axial.label: Grande Galerie — endless axial hang
grande-galerie-axial.walk_rule: Enter on axis and drift down the wide central lane toward the hero visible from the first step; at each bay, step sideways into the wall pocket to face a slot, then rejoin the flow, finally rounding the end-stopped hero to exit.
grande-galerie-axial.pacing_rule: Paired column cells pinch the 13-cell width every 4 rows into nine bays, and each bay's midpoint row carries a facing pair of wall slots — a metronome of stop-beats under one uninterrupted 33-cell sightline.

kanazawa-room-matrix.label: Kanazawa Free-Plan Room Matrix
kanazawa-room-matrix.museum: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa
kanazawa-room-matrix.walk_rule: Enter anywhere along the open top edge; parallel streets (west 3-wide, central 3-wide, east lane) and full-width cross streets loop around sealed room-boxes, and the central street's promised hero room dead-ends, sending the walker back into the field to choose an exit route.
kanazawa-room-matrix.pacing_rule: Seeing is quantized into rooms — pace is the number of boxes you elect to enter and leave through the street field, not distance walked; corridor-hung slots give the streets themselves exhibition weight between stops.

sainsbury-false-perspective-enfilade.label: Sainsbury Enfilade (false-perspective axis)
sainsbury-false-perspective-enfilade.walk_rule: Enter on-axis at the top and the hero is already visible 28 cells away through every door gap; the 3-wide central nave carries the flow straight to the raised hero chamber, while offset side doors peel viewers into 3-cell-wide cabinet rooms and return them to the axis one bay deeper.
sainsbury-false-perspective-enfilade.pacing_rule: Cross walls every 5-6 rows frame the vista and the door gaps narrow as you go (5, 5, 3, 3 cells) — a false perspective that makes the hero feel farther then suddenly near — with the final threshold stepping up onto a platform where the 3s altarpiece slot is end-stopped by the terminal wall and the exit turns off-axis, exactly as the wing hands you sideways to the bridge.

altes-rotunda-hub.label: Altes Rotunda Hub
altes-rotunda-hub.walk_rule: The walker enters at the top gap onto the x=7 axis, crosses the vestibule and the screen-wall door at row 5, passes the stair-hall antechamber into the rotunda's north door at row 10, and from the rotunda's four doors (rows 10/18 at x=7, row 14 at x=4/x=10) makes out-and-back loops into the flanking wing corridors before leaving by the south door and the bottom gap.
altes-rotunda-hub.pacing_rule: Stopping concentrates inside the rotunda ring (the hero at 14,7 and the four 1s statue niches against the chamfered corners) and at the 2s podiums pressed against the wing outer walls, while the x=7 spine and the row-14 cross-axis stay entirely slot-free, so a pausing viewer never blocks the through-path.

bilbao-atrium-radial.label: Bilbao Atrium Radial
bilbao-atrium-radial.walk_rule: Enter the top gap into the lobby, pass the center door into the 5-cell-wide atrium shaft and ride it south, stepping through single-cell side doors (rows 6/11/16 left, 7/12/17 right) into 3x4 gallery pockets and back to the shaft each time, then take the narrow row-19 door into the 13-cell-wide boat gallery, weave among its podiums past the central hero, and leave through the terrace to the bottom gap.
bilbao-atrium-radial.pacing_rule: All stopping happens one door off the spine — inside the six radiating pockets and around the flanked hero in the long gallery — while the atrium shaft itself holds no slots, so the lit center always carries through-flow and every pause is a fresh departure that never dams the walk.

chichu-buried-cells.label: Chichu Buried Cells
chichu-buried-cells.walk_rule: Follow the single 1-wide corridor of "1" cells through the dark; each time a 1-cell doorway opens in the "4" wall, step off the spine into the cell, circle its lone slot, and return to the spine before descending further.
chichu-buried-cells.pacing_rule: Long wall-bound compression between rooms, one work per release — the corridor stretches (4+ cells of pure passage) must always be longer than the room they deliver you into, except the final hero chamber.

dia-beacon-field.label: Dia:Beacon Field of Bays
dia-beacon-field.walk_rule: Enter on the center line and drift sideways between column strips: each strip of '1' floor bounded by the x=3/7/11 column rhythm is one artist's bay, and you cross freely between them anywhere a divider stub does not block.
dia-beacon-field.pacing_rule: No sequence — long slow parallel drifts down open bays with lateral crossings, pausing longest in the single hero bay where one monumental work owns the entire strip.

libeskind-void-axis.label: Libeskind Void Axis
libeskind-void-axis.walk_rule: Walk the switchbacks: each full-width wall forces a hard turn, the three sealed void chambers on the central columns are never enterable — pass them along their flanking corridors, let the dead-end pockets beside each void deliver you to a slot facing blank wall, and cross the void line only at the open turn rows.
libeskind-void-axis.pacing_rule: Long quiet flank runs beside sealed voids alternate with abrupt forced turns; slots stay sparse (about one per fifteen walkable cells) and cluster at void walls and dead ends, so absence sets the rhythm and the single hero is met against the largest void.

louisiana-pavilion-chain.label: Louisiana Pavilion Chain
louisiana-pavilion-chain.museum: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art, Humlebæk
louisiana-pavilion-chain.walk_rule: Alternate walled pavilion chambers with 1-wide glass-link corridors that jog sideways between them, so the walker crosses an empty slotless passage and changes heading before every new room.
louisiana-pavilion-chain.pacing_rule: Room, breath, room — each pavilion is a dense cluster of works, each link is deliberately empty, and the single hero plinth waits in the last pavilion, earned by the whole walk.

castelvecchio-endstop-pinch.label: Castelvecchio (pinch edit)
castelvecchio-endstop-pinch.walk_rule: Enter on the central axis and cross four rooms through aligned 3-wide door gaps, drifting to off-axis stop pockets as before; in the hero bay the east flank is now walled into a final stop pocket, so you circle the podium on the west and the only route onward runs along its lowered south rank, carrying you one to two cells beneath the statue before the off-axis side door releases you down the exit corridor.
castelvecchio-endstop-pinch.pacing_rule: The hero stays withheld behind four pause-and-drift cross walls exactly as in the ancestor, but the resolution is now a pinch: the pulled-in east wall and lowered south podium rank force the exit path directly under the statue, so the climax lands at close range and maximum angular size instead of a polite orbit around a distant ring.

provenance.diagnosis: withheld hero scores patience now, but climax magnitude is modest — heroDeg peaks small
provenance.edit: Pulled the hero bay east wall in across the podium rows and lowered the podium south rank, so the only path to the exit passes 1-2 cells beneath the statue at a spatial pinch.

kanazawa-matrix-vista.label: Kanazawa Matrix (vista edit)
kanazawa-matrix-vista.walk_rule: Enter anywhere along the open top edge; parallel streets still loop around sealed room-boxes, but the hero now stands where the central street crosses the mid cross-street — one straight vista from the door — while the old dead-end room withholds a last small work that sends the walker back into the field to choose an exit.
kanazawa-matrix-vista.pacing_rule: Seeing stays quantized into rooms you elect to enter, but one promise is granted up front: the hero grows steadily down the central axis to a climax at the crossing, and every room after it is a chosen digression rather than a search.

provenance.diagnosis: perfect tau, zero hero vista — promise/rank1 always 0
provenance.edit: Re-sited the 3s from the dead-end room at (8,21) to (8,14), the central-street / mid-cross-street crossing, leaving a 1s in the vacated dead-end — two cells changed, no walls touched.

mezquita-hypostyle.label: Mezquita Hypostyle
mezquita-hypostyle.walk_rule: Enter and lose the door: every aisle repeats every other aisle, so walk by drift, not axis — pick any corridor, turn when a slot breaks the column rhythm, and let the off-axis hero (the mihrab) find you deep in the southeast of the field; the exit is just another gap in the wall, met the same way.
mezquita-hypostyle.pacing_rule: Metronomic: a column every second cell sets a constant beat with no crescendo and no vista; slots are rests scattered off-symmetry within the beat, the single hero is one held note — density never varies, so all pacing comes from the walker's own turns.

pompidou-plateau-libre.label: Pompidou Plateau Libre
pompidou-plateau-libre.walk_rule: Enter onto the open plateau and see the hero immediately, dead ahead down the clear central spine. Walk the free field in any order — servicing bays wall the edges, podium slots drift past on both flanks — but every path bends toward the centre, where the hero stands fully in the round before the spine releases you to the exit.
pompidou-plateau-libre.pacing_rule: No enforced sequence: pacing is self-set on one open floor. The hero is met early by eye and late by body — visible from the threshold, reached mid-walk, re-seen from behind on the way out. Slot podiums alternate left-right at even intervals like structural bays, giving a loose rhythm without ever interrupting the plateau.

teshima-droplet.label: Teshima Droplet
teshima-droplet.walk_rule: one path only: enter at the gap, serpentine the long outdoor approach for over half the tile's length, pass through the narrow neck into the droplet chamber, circle the single work, leave by the far gap
teshima-droplet.pacing_rule: the approach is the decompression — no slots, no incident, just walking; then everything at once in one chamber and nothing after; slot density is the lowest in the corpus by design

uffizi-spine-ordered.label: Uffizi Spine (order edit)
uffizi-spine-ordered.walk_rule: Enter at the head of the east spine and walk the 3-wide corridor pulled forward by the hero visible on-axis 27 cells ahead; each side room now files its offerings down the door-side wall in the order the descent meets them, so dipping through the door bands never rewinds the sequence; turn west along the south corridor past the hero and exit on the enfilade axis.
uffizi-spine-ordered.pacing_rule: Podium statues still line the spine's inner wall in Vasari's bay rhythm, and each room's three pieces stack just inside the door band from top to bottom so the dealt order and the walked order stay in step; every pause sits off the clear lane, and the one mandated stop remains the raised dais step before the end-stopped hero.

provenance.diagnosis: tau swings to -0.6: row-major dealing disagrees with the U-walk's encounter order
provenance.edit: Moved the nine side-room slot cells from scattered interior positions to a top-to-bottom file just inside each room's door band (column 8, door rows), so row-major slot reading now tracks the U-walk's encounter order while spine podiums, hero, walls, and all slot counts stay untouched.

capuchin-crypt-corridor.label: Capuchin Crypt — corridor of refused rooms
capuchin-crypt-corridor.museum: Capuchin Crypt, Santa Maria della Concezione dei Cappuccini, Via Veneto, Rome
capuchin-crypt-corridor.architect: Capuchin friars under Cardinal Antonio Barberini; bones transferred from Via dei Lucchesi 1631, arrangements largely mid-18th century, accumulating burials 1500–1870
capuchin-crypt-corridor.circulation_type: Single-aisle one-way lateral procession: an unbranching corridor past six rooms that open onto it but are not entered
capuchin-crypt-corridor.mechanism: Flow and seeing are separated by a lip rather than a room: the walker is confined to a two-cell corridor while the collection occupies a raised mass four times its width, so every specimen is seen frontally, at a fixed unclosable distance, embedded in a continuous surface rather than standing free.
capuchin-crypt-corridor.not_a_museum: A museum gallery is a room you enter to be among the objects; here the only room you are permitted to enter is the one that contains no remains, and it holds the only object that stands on your own floor — so the building stages refusal of approach as its entire content, which no plinth-and-aisle gallery can do.
capuchin-crypt-corridor.walk_rule: One two-cell corridor runs the full length of the tile. No branch, no loop, no return, no choice — the body enters at the top and leaves at the bottom having walked a tube. Every bone chapel opens to the right as a raised mass the walker can only look into: the '2' lip at the corridor edge is the barrier, and each slot sits one step beyond it, so the reach is always one cell short. The walker's floor is 60 of 390 cells; the collection's volume is four times larger and entirely off-limits. Exactly one threshold opens — the walkable side-room at rows 7-10 — and it is the only room in the tile whose object is a floor slot standing on the walker's own floor, with no lip and no podium between.
capuchin-crypt-corridor.pacing_rule: Six openings in thirty rows, each sealed off from the next by a one-row wall pier, so the corridor closes and reopens six times. The framing rooms (rows 2-5, rows 24-27) are four rows deep; the three taxonomic chapels between them are three rows each — a fast even drumbeat of one-bone-type-per-room, skulls then pelvises then femurs. Chapel depth swells backwards as you go (six cells, seven, six, eight, eight) while the corridor never widens by a single cell. The hero is stopped at exactly the same lip as the femur wall: content escalates, access never does.

caracalla-thermal-axis.label: Caracalla thermal axis — mirrored wings, palindromic return, unapproachable core
caracalla-thermal-axis.architect: Commissioned by Septimius Severus / completed under Caracalla, architect unrecorded; built AD 212–216/217, Severan imperial Rome
caracalla-thermal-axis.circulation_type: Mirrored axial enfilade of thermal states — two identical wings flanking one shared central spine, alternating split/merge, terminating in a domed rotunda that blocks the axis and forces a retrograde back through the same rooms in reverse temperature order
caracalla-thermal-axis.mechanism: Flow runs on the axis and seeing runs on the walls: every basin, niche and statue is set into the flanking thickness so the body never has to stop facing forward, while the one thing standing on the axis — the domed hot core — cannot be entered at all, only committed to on one side and orbited at a podium's remove, so approach and vision are held permanently at right angles.
caracalla-thermal-axis.not_a_museum: A bath stages a body that is being changed — heated, scraped, plunged, cooled — so the room itself is the exhibit and the objects are incidental furniture you pass while becoming something else; a gallery can only ever stage a body that stays the same and accumulates looks.
caracalla-thermal-axis.walk_rule: Walk the spine and let it keep changing your number: broad merged halls (portico, frigidarium) put one body on the axis, then the pool and the rotunda split you into two mirrored aisles that cannot see across. At the core you must commit to a side — there is no crossing the centre line — and you re-merge only after passing it. Past the core the tile is its own reflection: the same three bands in reverse order, so the exit walk is the entry walk read backwards at a different temperature.
caracalla-thermal-axis.pacing_rule: Nothing stands on the axis except the one hero, and the hero is unreachable — every other slot is pushed into the flanking wall thickness as a niche, so the body reads sideways while moving forward and never stops to face a thing head-on. Split bands are silent: the natatio and rotunda aisles carry no slots at all, because a body crossing a state should have nothing to look at. Merged bands carry the podia, one pair per hall, always at the outer wall. Dwell should climb through the pinch, spike in the orbit where the hero is passed twice at one podium's remove and touched never, then decay through the mirrored half, where the same rooms are met a second time and should be given roughly half the time — the return is recognition, not discovery.

katsura-miegakure-circuit.label: Katsura miegakure circuit
katsura-miegakure-circuit.museum: Katsura Imperial Villa (Katsura Rikyū), Kyoto — the chisen-kaiyū-shiki (pond stroll) garden and its circuit path
katsura-miegakure-circuit.architect: Prince Hachijō Toshihito and Prince Toshitada, with the Kobori Enshū circle credited by tradition; built in phases c. 1615–1662 (early Edo)
katsura-miegakure-circuit.circulation_type: Forced single-thread serpentine circuit around an uncrossable water body — three descending/ascending legs, baffled sightlines (miegakure), one obligatory turn-chamber at the far apex, and a released return
katsura-miegakure-circuit.mechanism: Seeing is rationed by walking: the pond is a hole in the walkable world, so the body must go down one shore, along the beach, and back up the other before it can reach anything, and the corridor is baffled so that every straight run dies against a wall or mound within six cells — you look down at your feet, turn, and only in the turn does anything open.
katsura-miegakure-circuit.not_a_museum: A museum gallery lets you see the object from the door and decide whether to approach; here the hero sits seven cells from the entrance in plan and seventy-nine steps away on foot, and the only door between the up-leg and the down-leg is the cell beside it — you cannot browse, skip, or approach frontally, you can only arrive.
katsura-miegakure-circuit.walk_rule: One forced thread, no branches. Enter top-centre on a narrow three-cell approach (the Miyukimichi), walk four cells and hit a wall: the Sumiyoshi-pine blocker turns you west along the tile's one long entry traverse. Descend the west shore (cols 1-2) for twenty-three rows against a wall of alternating baffles and mounds — no straight run over five cells, so the head is down and the next turn is never visible. At the bottom the shore terrace (rows 26-27) runs east under the pond; a podium stands in the middle of it, so even the beach must be walked around. Ascend the east shore (cols 10-11), equally baffled. At the top the corridor narrows into a four-cell chamber (row 5) that is the ONLY connection between the up-leg and the down-leg: the hero podium stands in the wall you turn against, and every body that leaves this tile has stood beside it. Then the release — the outbound leg (col 13) is a single-file descent with only three jogs and the tile's longest sightline, twenty-five rows back down to the exit gate at bottom-right. Total walked ≈112 cells for a tile 32 rows tall.
katsura-miegakure-circuit.pacing_rule: Content sits on the inbound legs and is never frontal. Podiums go INSIDE the two-wide corridors so the body squeezes past with the head turned (rows 10 and 12); floor stones sit in the path itself (rows 17, 24, 25) and are read looking down. Never place two slots within four rows of each other on the same leg — the baffles, not the objects, set the rhythm, and an object every fourth turn is the correct density. The shore terrace gets exactly one podium, standing in the open where the head finally comes up. The 3s hero is reserved for the turn-chamber and must never be duplicated in spirit: nothing else in the tile may be approachable head-on. The outbound leg carries at most one item — it is the walk home, and its job is to make the tile's length felt rather than filled.

labrouste-stack-hall.label: Labrouste stack hall — twin nave over a closed magasin
labrouste-stack-hall.circulation_type: committed twin-nave spine — six parallel aisles that never cross, hemmed by tables, with the collection sealed at the walls and below the floor
labrouste-stack-hall.mechanism: The walk is separated from the seeing by a solid centre: a body enters off-axis at the stair corner, commits to one of six longitudinal aisles it cannot leave, and moves the whole length hemmed by reading tables with the book-presses two rows outboard behind grilles — the only object it can actually reach is the delivery desk on axis at the far end, where the hidden ground-floor magasin surfaces.
labrouste-stack-hall.not_a_museum: A museum gallery puts the collection in your path so you approach it; this plan puts the collection behind you, above you and beneath you, and gives you instead a long file of places to SIT — the thing you came for is fetched from a room you never enter, so the tile stages waiting and passage rather than looking.
labrouste-stack-hall.walk_rule: Enter off-axis at the corner (the stair does not take space from the room), cross a 3-row head band, then COMMIT: the centre spine is solid for 25 rows, so a body picks one of six parallel aisles and cannot change nave until the spine terminates in the delivery desk. Exit is on the centre axis, so every traversal turns from edge to middle and passes the one reachable object last.
labrouste-stack-hall.pacing_rule: Bay period 5. Table rows break laterally on rows 8/13/18/23 (within a nave only, never across the spine) — that is the arch bay. Wall book-presses fire on rows 6/11/16/21/26, reading-table lamps on rows 5/15/25, so the two slot families alternate on off-beats and a slot passes the shoulder every 2–3 steps. NO floor slots at all: nothing in this building stands in your path, everything is furniture you go around or shelving you cannot reach. The single 3s sits on the spine axis at row 29 — the counter where the hidden stack surfaces.

mengoni-glazed-thoroughfare.label: Mengoni Glazed Thoroughfare — arcade street with octagonal crossing
mengoni-glazed-thoroughfare.architect: Giuseppe Mengoni — competition design 1861, built 1865–1877 (Mengoni died in a fall from the scaffolding days before the 1878 inauguration)
mengoni-glazed-thoroughfare.circulation_type: Thoroughfare — a glazed public street, cruciform in plan, open at both ends of the long arm onto two city squares, with an octagonal rotunda at the crossing; no terminus, no route, no ticket
mengoni-glazed-thoroughfare.mechanism: Flow is never interrupted for seeing: the goods sit behind a continuous glazed band at the walker's shoulder, so attention is paid at walking speed and in the periphery, and the plan's single concession to stopping is the octagonal crossing, where the band steps back, four ways meet, and an intersection becomes a room you can stand still in.
mengoni-glazed-thoroughfare.not_a_museum: It is a public street with two open ends and a destination beyond itself, so the walk owes nothing to what is displayed — no one can be made to finish it, and the display has to earn a turned head from a body already going somewhere else.
mengoni-glazed-thoroughfare.walk_rule: The walker is passing through, not visiting. Both ends are portals onto somewhere else, so there is no terminus and no reward for completion; the walkable channel runs unbroken from row 0 to row 32 and the body never has to turn around. Display is lateral and continuous — a raised glazed band pressed against both walls at the shoulder, approached obliquely at walking speed, never frontally. Nothing in the arms can be circled or stood in front of squarely. The one exception is the octagon at mid-tile, where the band steps back to the chamfered faces, the room widens to the full frame, two lateral arms open and immediately meet their own end walls, and the single hero object sits dead centre in the walking line so the walk must part around it. That detour is the only stop the plan asks for.
mengoni-glazed-thoroughfare.pacing_rule: In the arms: one wall slot every two rows, alternating left and right (rows 1,5,9 left / 3,7 right, mirrored south), with plain raised band filling every row in between — the band is never empty, so the walker registers merchandise as a texture and the slots as a beat. The head swings, the feet do not stop. Nothing sits in the middle of the street. At the crossing the beat breaks: four chamfer podiums at the diagonal corners (rows 12 and 20), two exedra podiums at the dead ends of the lateral arms (row 16, both frame edges) — the only slots in the tile a body can walk straight at — four floor medallions quartering the rotunda floor (rows 14 and 18), and one hero at centre with walkable cells on all four sides. Ratio matters: twenty-two slots you slide past, three you can face, one you can orbit.

mesdag-panorama-drum.label: Panorama drum — one platform, a ring you cannot enter
mesdag-panorama-drum.museum: Panorama Mesdag, Zeestraat 65, The Hague — purpose-built panorama rotunda housing the Panorama van Scheveningen (1881), the oldest panorama in the world still on its original site
mesdag-panorama-drum.architect: Gerardus Klomp (1834–1882) designed and developed the rotunda, 1880–81, for the Belgian Société Anonyme des Panoramas; the faux terrain (artificial dune) inside was designed by architect Cornelis Johan Laarman (1844–1889); the Zeestraat entrance building and garden between street and drum reworked 1910–11 under Mesdag. Opened 1 August 1881.
mesdag-panorama-drum.circulation_type: Single-station rotunda: a dark, slotless approach corridor, a stair, one radial trench through the artificial dune, one fixed central viewing platform, and a second trench out — the visitor stops walking and rotates instead. The work is the enclosing wall and is separated from the body by an uncrossable raised terrain at every point of the circle.
mesdag-panorama-drum.mechanism: The plan converts locomotion into rotation: all walkable ground is compressed into a narrow blind approach and a 3×3 platform, while the entire seeing-surface is pushed to a fixed radius behind a continuous band of raised faux terrain, so the only way to change the view is to turn on the spot — distance to the work is a constant the body cannot alter.
mesdag-panorama-drum.not_a_museum: A gallery rewards walking with more and closer looking; this building removes approach as an option entirely — the largest thing in it is met from one immovable foot position, at one distance, forever, which is a spatial argument no room full of approachable objects can make.
mesdag-panorama-drum.walk_rule: Enter narrow and blind. The approach is two cells wide, dog-legs once, compresses to one cell, and carries ZERO slots for eight rows — there is deliberately nothing to see while walking. It pierces the drum wall as a one-cell trench with raised dune on both sides, so the chamber is invisible until the last step. The body emerges onto the 3×3 platform at its north-west corner and must cross to the south-east corner to find the descent: the only motion the platform grants is a turn. Everything else inside the drum is raised terrain — the hero is two cells from the feet, with one band of sand between, and cannot be reached from any cell in the tile. Exactly one small slot (the 1s on the platform) is touchable; the enormous one never is.
mesdag-panorama-drum.pacing_rule: This is a terminal beat, not a sequence. Give the tunnels no camera stations and no dwell at all — they are pure duration. Give the platform 3–4× a normal gallery stop and let the sightline sweep a full 360° from a fixed foot position; the hero sits on the axis opposite the entry trench so it is first met by turning, never by approaching. Do not chain two of these back to back and do not splice a drum into a fast run — put at least one ordinary walked tile on each side, or the darkness reads as loading rather than as preparation.

sando-threshold-run.label: Sandō — the gate is the exhibit
sando-threshold-run.museum: Sandō (processional approach): Senbon Torii at Fushimi Inari Taisha, Kyoto — read together with the Naikū sandō at Ise Jingū, Mie
sando-threshold-run.architect: Anonymous and accreted. Fushimi Inari founded 711 CE; the torii tunnels are donated gates accumulated from the Edo period (1600s) onward and continuously replaced by Hasegawa Kōmuten. Ise Jingū's sandō, Uji Bridge and torii are rebuilt from scratch every 20 years under Shikinen Sengū (since 690 CE).
sando-threshold-run.circulation_type: Single-file processional threshold run — a repeated pinch-and-release rhythm of gates, with a two-lane fork whose branches are interchangeable, ending at a screened terminus the path passes beside rather than arrives at
sando-threshold-run.mechanism: Flow and seeing are collapsed into one act: the corridor is squeezed to a single cell at every gate so the only thing a body can look at is the frame it is currently passing through, and the one object that would reward stopping is set behind a screen where it can be seen but never reached.
sando-threshold-run.not_a_museum: A gallery gives you objects to halt in front of; this plan gives you a cadence that only exists while you keep moving and then withholds its hero entirely — the content is the interval between thresholds, which no hang of works on a wall can produce.
sando-threshold-run.walk_rule: Single file, always. The corridor pinches to one cell at every gate row and there is no bay wide enough to step aside in; a body behind you cannot pass. At row 9 the path splits into two identical one-cell lanes with a solid spine between them — commit to one, you cannot cross back until row 21. The hero at row 29 is passed on the right shoulder behind a screen and is never faced; the walk continues straight out the bottom without turning to it.
sando-threshold-run.pacing_rule: The sixteen 1s throats are ONE artifact instanced sixteen times, never sixteen different works — vary only scale and hue along the run (small and tight at rows 2–8, widest and heaviest at rows 23–27). Both fork lanes carry the same five instances so the choice is genuinely empty. The three 2s are the only stoppable objects and are votive duplicates of each other, deliberately unremarkable. The single 3s gets its stop pocket only through the 2s screen at row 29: it must be lit and legible from row 29 col 6 and physically unreachable from anywhere.

thoronet-circumambulation-void.label: Le Thoronet cloister — the walk that will not cross the middle
thoronet-circumambulation-void.museum: Le Thoronet Abbey cloister, Provence (Var), France
thoronet-circumambulation-void.architect: Anonymous Cistercian master masons of the Order; abbey 1160–1190, cloister galleries begun c. 1175 and completed early 13th century
thoronet-circumambulation-void.circulation_type: Closed circumambulation around an impassable void — peripheral-only movement, bidirectional, no chord across the centre; the arcade is a 1.5 m-thick pierced wall that lets the centre be seen but never entered
thoronet-circumambulation-void.mechanism: The garth is literally impassable, so the tile offers no chord: to advance twenty-eight rows you walk seventy-odd cells around the outside of a square you may never enter, while the arcade meters that void into pier–bay–pier–bay so the centre arrives only in slices, and a rock outcrop from the hillside pinches the west walk to single file where the ground drops.
thoronet-circumambulation-void.not_a_museum: A gallery guarantees you the whole collection along one route, but the ring gives you a choice of direction and hides the other half — the single hero, the hexagonal lavabo, sits on one arm only, so half of all walkers never meet it, and the thing at the centre of the composition is nothing at all.
thoronet-circumambulation-void.walk_rule: Enter by the north-east door and leave by the south-west; the centre is void so no step may cross it, and the two mirror-equal arms of the ring (north-then-west, or east-then-south) both reach the exit. The direction chosen decides which half of the contents is never met — the lavabo hero sits on the north arm alone. All four galleries stay continuous, as in the building; nothing is walled off to force the detour, the emptiness in the middle does all the forcing.
thoronet-circumambulation-void.pacing_rule: Along the whole inner edge the arcade alternates pier (4) and bay (2) without pause — solid, opening, solid, opening — so the garth is metered rather than given whole; a slot sits in roughly every third bay, and the podium slots face the void so what stands in the opening is read against nothing. The floor stays almost bare: six floor slots across seventy-six cells of gallery, Cistercian sparsity as a rate, not a mood. One pinch at rows 15–16 (the hillside rock at the seven-step level change) narrows the west walk to a single cell, the only place the body cannot pass two abreast.

numbers.name: Cloister side (average)
numbers.value: ~30 m, in the shape of an elongated trapezoid, not a square
numbers.source_note: fr.wikipedia + en.wikipedia: 'mesure en moyenne 30 mètres de côté', 'in the shape of an elongated trapezoid' following the slope down toward the river

numbers.name: Arcade wall thickness
numbers.value: 1.5 m, pierced with twin round-arched bays on a thick central column, oculus above
numbers.source_note: fr.wikipedia: 'baies géminées percées dans un mur d'un mètre cinquante d'épaisseur'

numbers.name: Level change between galleries
numbers.value: seven steps; the south gallery sits lower than the north, hillside rock left as part of the fabric
numbers.source_note: fr.wikipedia: 'sept marches'; en.wikipedia notes rock from the hillside becoming part of the architecture

numbers.name: Lavabo
numbers.value: hexagonal pavilion, five-sided stone dome on six ogives, upper basin 1.35 m diameter, sixteen taps, two doors
numbers.source_note: fr.wikipedia; en.wikipedia places it 'in the cloister in front of what had been the entrance to the refectory'

numbers.name: Galleries
numbers.value: four, barrel-vaulted (east gallery slightly pointed); built 1175 → early 13th c.; church ~40 × 20 m alongside
numbers.source_note: fr.wikipedia + en.wikipedia; south gallery oldest, then east, north, west
